definition: The strongest honest version of an argument you may disagree with, built from the best available evidence, as opposed to a 'straw man' that is easy to knock down.
A grid that places each risk by its likelihood (x-axis) and impact (y-axis), usually scored 1-5 each; the product of the two ranks which risks deserve attention first.
A measurable signal that tends to move before the outcome you care about, such as hyperscaler capex guidance moving before NVIDIA's orders do.

Buyers placing the same order with several suppliers, or ordering more than they need, during a shortage to secure allocation; the excess vanishes when supply catches up and can make demand look stronger than it is.

An electricity market in which a grid operator pays generators (in $ per MW-day) to be available years ahead; PJM's auction price is a public gauge of how scarce firm power is in the largest US data-center region.

Making the sale of one product conditional on buying another, for example GPUs only with the vendor's own networking; it can breach competition law when the seller has market power in the first product.
Share price divided by the next twelve months' or next fiscal year's expected earnings per share (equivalently market value divided by expected net income).
Working backwards from today's market value to the growth or margins it implies, instead of forecasting cash flows and deriving a value; in its simplest form P/E = 1 / (cost of equity - growth).
A public benchmark of PyTorch operations, grouped in three difficulty levels, used to test whether AI models can write GPU kernels that are correct and faster than PyTorch's own.
The number of years over which a company spreads the cost of an asset such as a GPU server; a longer life lowers annual depreciation and raises reported profit.
